messages:
Sachin: quick signal — noticed a cluster of 429s in prod after we migrated a service account from project `proj-88` -> org `org-14`. Telemetry shows request rate attributed to proj-88 dropping, but quotas still being charged there. any ideas? :thinking:

Maria: hmm. did we rebind the service account keys or just changed the owner in the console? two different flows.

Sachin: console change only — clicked "transfer ownership" in the UI, no key rotation. infra-bot logs show the same token used, but our attribution layer switched owner tag to org-14. quotas still point to proj-88 id. mismatch somewhere.

Jon: if the token didn't rotate, quota attribution should remain where the token was minted. We currently attribute by token_id -> original_project mapping in the auth DB. UI transfer should either mint a new delegated token or update mappings atomically; looks like UI updated owner metadata but not quota mapping.

Kevin: that explains 429s. Requests are being routed to project quota enforcement which still thinks the consumer is proj-88; but billing/telemetry show org-14 as owner because we changed console metadata. We need a single source of truth.

Leliana: options:
- update quota mapping when ownership is transferred (mutate token->project mapping)
- force rotation on transfer (mint new token under new owner)
- keep mapping immutable and add aliasing layer that requests can opt into

Maria: rotation is safest security-wise but bad UX. We discussed forced rotation in previous threads and teams hated the forced downtime.

Jon: we could do a gradual UX: prompt to rotate, allow skip with checkbox that creates an explicit mapping override (audit log) and shows clear warning about quota attribution.

Kevin: telemetry request: we should add a stable claim in delegated tokens: `owner_claim` containing immutable origin (like `proj:proj-88`) and a separate `current_owner` meta in console. Then logs/metrics can pick authoritative field for billing vs display.

Sachin: can we sign that claim so it can't be forged? e.g., JWT with `iss=redwood`, `sub=token-xxx`, `owner=proj-88`.

Jon: signing helps, but if we allow owner to be changed without rotation the claim becomes stale. If we want immutable owner we must mint new token or update claim by rotation.

ops-bot: FYI deploy-bot started rolling out auth-service v3 to canary:auth-canary-2 (2021-11-22T10:01Z)

Maria: telemetry concern: adding owner fields to logs is great, but we must ensure no PII or customer identifiers leak in lower-tier logs. we should tag as `owner_id` and use hashed ID in public dashboards.

Kevin: agreed. proposal:
1) on transfer, show console modal with 2 options: "rotate token (recommended)" or "transfer metadata only (advanced)". If advanced chosen, create mapping override with audit entry and TTL=7d. During TTL requests are eligible for fallback routing.
2) add `origin_owner` claim embedded in tokens on issuance (immutable). If user rotates, new token gets new claim.
3) telemetry: add `token_origin` (hashed) + `effective_owner` (hashed) tags. Billing uses `token_origin` by default unless explicit mapping override exists.
4) fallback: when quota 429 occurs and mapping override present, try org-reserved pool for up to TTL seconds before hard 429.

Leliana: TTL=7d is arbitrary, what about 0 (immediate rollback) vs 30d? we should test with small sample. also need to show explicit knob in Dedicated configs.

Sachin: SRE: if we auto-fallback to org pool, risk of double-charging or unexpected throttling for other orgs. need strict guardrails and metrics.

Jon: implementation notes:
- auth-service: add `owner_claim` to JWT at issue time
- metadata-service: maintain `token_id -> billing_project` map (mutable only via explicit override)
- quota-enforcer: check override map first, then token origin
- console: transfer flow with modal + audit entry

Maria: UX copy draft for modal: "Transfer token ownership — rotating keys is recommended. If you choose to transfer without rotation, requests will route under the new org for display but billing may still be charged to the original project until the override TTL expires. This is advanced and requires admin consent."

Kevin: metrics/dashboard asks: add new panels: `qps by token_origin (hashed)`, `qps by effective_owner`, `override_count`, `fallback_uses`. Also add alert for sudden spike in `override_uses` (suspicious transfer activity).

infra-bot: perf-test results uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-ci/auth-override-canary/run-21/results.json

Leliana: security review: blocked until we prove audit trail preserves who initiated transfer and that we never leak raw project ids in low-security logs. Also need to ensure KMS keys used to sign claims are rotated and audited.

Sachin: decision: implement binding override TTL=7d by default behind feature flag `auth.transfer_override`. feature flag rollout: start with internal orgs + 3 beta customers. console modal + audit log required. telemetry hashed ids only. RFC by EOW from @Jon.

Jon: I'll draft RFC and include sequence diagram + DB migration plan. assigning to myself. Will tag eng-sre and product for rollout plan.

Maria: thanks — can someone own the dashboard tickets? @Kevin? :raised_hands: 

Kevin: on it. I'll create dashboards and alerts, and sync with SRE next week.

Sachin: nice. follow-ups: add an item to private-deploy checklist about token rotation, and add automated smoke for quota attribution during canary.

infra-bot: ticket created: AUTH-3421 "transfer ownership flow v1" assigned to Jon, priority P2

Jon: great. I'll post RFC link here when ready.
